title: Investigate existing software
summary: Choose a focused source, architecture or binary investigation and retain the evidence behind each explanation.

sections.label: Use this workflow
sections.text: Use before changing an unfamiliar system, investigating behavior or diagnosing a defect. Begin with a question and target revision. Read source directly when sufficient. A graph or native analysis provider is an optional way to obtain evidence.

sections.label: Inputs
items: Question, expected behavior and permitted target.
Repository revision or binary identity, relevant platform and available tools.
Time or token budget and the evidence needed to choose the next action.

sections.label: Repository contributions
rows: Explore generated code relationships and explanations.
Sample nodes, dependency edges and summaries against the same source revision.
Curate architectural responsibilities and relationships as C4/OKF Markdown.
Review the first scan, boundaries and ownership. Reconcile the map after refactors.
Navigate symbols and references when the host lacks an equivalent semantic tool.
Confirm the language/backend and inspect returned definitions and call sites.
Investigate application artifacts, behavior and native binaries.
Check the selected provider, target identity, limits and incomplete results.
Inspect inferred types, addresses and pseudocode. Reproduced behavior remains separate.

sections.label: Procedure
items: State one behavior or ownership question and pin the target.
Inspect the entry point and relevant path using the smallest sufficient available tool.
Record file/symbol or binary-address evidence, observations and inferred explanations separately.
If using a generated graph or architecture map, check a sample of relationships and omitted boundaries against source.
Investigate contradictions and missing evidence before proposing a change. Stop at unavailable inputs or the agreed budget.
Deliver the explanation, affected responsibilities, supporting anchors and unresolved questions to the next step.

sections.label: Outputs
sections.text: A source-linked investigation note and, where useful, a reviewed map or impact list tied to the inspected revision.

sections.label: Acceptance checks
items: Every material explanation identifies observed source or binary evidence.
Generated descriptions and decompiled code are not labelled original source or complete architecture.
Partial analysis, timeouts and uninspected boundaries remain visible.
A diagnosis is distinguished from a tested repair.

sections.label: Illustrative example
sections.text: To investigate a saved-filter bug, trace the request from UI to persistence, then check whether the default filter is dropped on reload. A graph may help locate the path. Expected output is an anchored explanation and a reproduction plan. No investigation or repair has run in this example.

basis: Inspected repository documentation and recommended Atlas procedure. Examples are illustrative.
confidence: Moderate for the scoped source contributions. Project fit and workflow outcomes remain unverified.

catalog.applicability: Choose a focused source, architecture or binary investigation and retain the evidence behind each explanation.
catalog.limits: Reading guidance does not install a repository, select a tool, execute a workflow or establish a passing result. Use actual project versions, commands and evidence.

claims.text: Ghidra documents disassembly, decompilation, graphing and scripting for compiled-code analysis.
Groma documents a scanned and curated C4 architecture map stored as OKF Markdown.
